svg.title: TOPAK G4 — The command-chain overlay declares its adversaries, its trusted-base rows and its assumptions of use
svg.desc: ADR-0068 is the overlay's declaration of what it trusts and assumes, as ADR-0045's Annex B is the reference's: fourteen adversaries with what bounds each and what is left, twelve trusted-base rows classed by failure direction, ten assumptions of use, and what the nine records beside it give up. The corpus's adversary is the agent; this deployment adds adversaries that attack links, hardware and planes, and puts a trusted component on every vehicle (Context). ADR-0068 is Proposed and has not been revised: its Status note still says "nothing here is modelled, checked or built" and its §6 says "no module is written", while the TLA+ modules of ADR-0059 to ADR-0066 were written, checked and proved on 2026.11.10 and those records' R1 rows cite them. Where this diagram names a module property, that is its own cross-reference, marked as such, and not the record's text.
svg.text: TOPAK · G4

text.tspan: The command-chain overlay declares its adversaries, its trusted-base rows and its assumptions of use

svg.text: ADR-0068 is the overlay's declaration of what it trusts and assumes, as ADR-0045's Annex B is the reference's: fourteen adversaries with what bounds each and what is left, twelve trusted-base rows classed by failure direction, ten assumptions of use, and what the nine records beside it give up. The corpus's adversary is the agent; this deployment adds adversaries that attack links, hardware and planes, and puts a trusted component on every vehicle

(Context). ADR-0068 is Proposed and has not been revised: its Status note still says "nothing here is modelled, checked or built" and its §6 says "no module is written", while the TLA+ modules of ADR-0059 to ADR-0066 were written, checked and proved on 2026.11.10 and those records' R1 rows cite them. Where this diagram names a module property, that is its own cross-reference, marked as such, and not the record's text.

text.tspan: the modules of ADR-0059 to ADR-0066

svg.text: Proposed means nothing here is in force, and no record of the overlay is ratified. C2 applies: ADR-0045 holds that an undeclared row is false, so §2 is a claim that these rows are all the overlay adds to the trusted base. C1, C3 and C4 do not apply on the drafter's reading while this is an overlay ⟨Q11⟩. The custodian asked for a threat model ⟨3⟩ and answered ⟨Q9⟩ and ⟨Q11⟩; every other choice is the drafter's, and so are the row and assumption ids. ADR-0045 was not re-read beyond its refused rows
and finding 2 (provenance note). No row has been tested against a vehicle (Status note). One author, one day, and no vehicle (Consequences).

text.tspan: What exists that ADR-0068 does not say: the modules of ADR-0059 to ADR-0066 (the diagram's note, not the record's text)
ADR-0068 has not been revised to say the modules exist

svg.text: The record as it stands: its Status note says "Nothing here is modelled, checked or built", and §6 says of its third condition "Not met: no module is
written." Its History has one row, the initial draft, Proposed.
Since then, the same day: TLA+ modules for ADR-0059 to ADR-0066 were written, checked by TLC and proved with TLAPS, and each of those records
gained an R1 row citing its module (ADR-0067's R1 follows ADR-0063's; it has no module). ADR-0068 has no R1.
So this diagram draws the record as it stands, with its words "not met" and "no module is written", and says beside them, in teal and dashed, what the
modules now state. Nothing in a teal dashed frame is ADR-0068's.
The modules are of the specification. None of these words is said of running code: the floor stage federation is not written and the reference is not built.
ADR-0068 itself, a declaration, has no module.
Eight modules, 2026.11.10 (summary lines of each results, proof-results and proof-cert-results file)

Each proof module: "a proved obligation is a theorem of the module under its assumptions and the hypotheses the statement names"; mutations and witnesses stay with TLC. The module headers name findings against their records, and the R1 revisions took them. A property under a premise is drawn with its premise (the last column of §1's
table, below).

text.tspan: The planes above, to the root

svg.text: Each plane is seated by its parent's promotion under a charter it can only narrow, and is fenced by
every plane above it (ADR-0059 §1, §6).
A plane is a havoc issuer, bounded by its charter (ADR-0059 §4).
The anchor's custody is declared per deployment (ADR-0025) and is out of scope (§1).

text.tspan: A commanded plane: the intent boundary

svg.text: People are seated at it. The last commanded plane above a group of vehicles orders the authorizing admit of every effect (ADR-0060
A reversible effect is admitted as an intent, a charter for one round. An irreversible one is admitted itself, one at a time.
It reads the autonomous plane's record and answers with watermarks; a plane may have K_up effects outstanding and no more
T-0068-5 the intent boundary's reading: trust root for the watermark.
Order intents: the first by the tally that promoted the mesh, each later one by one operator (ADR-0060 §2).
TM7 · an insider with a key: whatever that seat may do. Bounded by attribution; an operator's add needs a live peer
Composes and signs each irreversible act: the only seat that reaches an irreversible entry (ADR-0066 §1–§3).
TM7: a wrong act by a release person is recorded and not prevented.
TM9 · deception of perception: a deceived person at a release seat is a semantic failure. Nothing here sees it.

text.tspan: The link above the plane, and the radios

svg.text: Jams, drops, delays, replays, injects. Cuts the link above a plane; cuts vehicles from their plane, making them alone; delays a revocation; blocks every irreversible effect.
Certificates stop forgery. Fences and sequence numbers stop replay. K_up bounds what a delay buys, in effects, and an intent's named tick stops a withheld one from starting late (ADR-0063, ADR-0064).
Loss only subtracts (T-0068-11, delegated): a plane cut off above stops granting before K_up, and a vehicle cut off from its plane loses its lease.
intents, release acts, fences, watermarks
the plane's record, and seals
Byzantine agreement with signed certificates, seven replicas tolerating two captured (ADR-0061 §1). T-0068-12 stands in place of the replica row there.
Defined by one absence: its log takes nothing that changes authority. It cannot seat, promote or release (ADR-0060 §3).
TM4 · compromised replicas, fewer than a third: lie to the others.
TM5 · a captured plane: a quorum of its replicas, which here means that share of its vehicles. Issues any lease within its charter, ignores fences, falsifies its log.
Shrinks only along a schedule its charter voted, down to a capture floor, each step ordered by a certificate of the membership it replaces (ADR-0061 §3, §4).
TM6 · a partitioned mesh: two groups each believing it is the plane. A certificate needs a quorum of the current membership, so at most one side grants.
TM12 · attrition: vehicles destroyed, or silenced until their replicas are dropped. At the archetype's size, four losses one at a time or two at once.
Ticks numbered from the charter, each signed by a certificate of replicas on their own clocks; every interval is a count of ticks from a named tick (ADR-0064
T-0068-3 the plane's clocks, taken together: trust root for the duration bound only.
TM14 · clock faults among the replicas: a slow clock holds an intent open, and a fast one ends it early.

text.tspan: A vehicle: a governor and a stack (ADR-0062 §1)

svg.text: Each loss is one replica fewer, and the plane walks down the schedule its
charter voted (ADR-0061 §3).
Below the capture floor the plane ends and every survivor is alone. An
adversary that can silence vehicles gets the floor's tolerance from the start.
Planning, perception, any model. Byzantine, as ADR-0007 has it (ADR-0062 §1).
TM1 · the stack: requests anything, at any time.
TM9: made wrong about the world. The premise already assumes it; perception never adds authority.

text.tspan: Peer topics, promoted with the mesh (ADR-0065 §1–§4)

svg.text: A send is an effect, permitted and never ordered. Receipt is ingress, labelled untrusted and by its topic. Nobody is addressed, and nothing a peer originates is ever an enabling condition. The governor holds the radio, so a stack cannot make its own vehicle alone (ADR-0062 §1).

text.tspan: An autonomous plane: seven replicas under Byzantine agreement, one on each vehicle's governor, below the intent boundary (ADR-0060 §3, ADR-0061 §1)

svg.text: The picture is the diagram's placement of §1's rows, not a figure in the record. Each adversary sits on what it attacks; the table below has every column. Out of scope (§1): destruction other than its effect on a quorum, which is TM12; attacks on sensors other than TM8 and TM9; traffic analysis; and the anchor's custody, which ADR-0025 declares per deployment.

text.tspan: §1 · Fourteen adversaries, each with what bounds it and what is left ⟨3⟩

text.tspan: The diagram's cross-reference, not ADR-0068's: a module header names the property; checked and proved 2026.11.10

svg.text: Out of scope (§1): the destruction of vehicles or planes, other than its effect on a quorum, which is TM12; attacks on sensors other than as TM8 and TM9; what an adversary learns by watching which planes and vehicles talk; and the security of the anchor's custody, which ADR-0025 declares per deployment.

The last column is the diagram's. A cell is empty where no module header names a property for that bound: TM4 (every module takes a commit certificate as unforgeable, and Membership abstracts PBFT to its certificate, so ADR-0061's "PBFT is read" is not met), TM7, TM8, TM9, TM10, and TM11 (Alone's LocalNeverWaits and Release's ReleaseNeverCoupled say nothing waits on an Observer, which bounds no collusion). A property stated under a premise says so. The Consequences say three adversaries have
"nothing" in the bounding column; two are bounded by nothing (TM8, TM11), and TM13's cell begins "Nothing a peer originates enables anything", which is a bound.

Trust root for an entry whose extent is a distance or a region

an owner (Findings 1). PlaneClock counts an extent in ticks: "distance and region are measurements (ADR-0068)"

svg.text: Cedar and the Wasm engine on the vehicle
Existing rows, instantiated on every vehicle
As those rows say
The record names no ids. In ADR-0045's Annex A the Cedar engine is T-0045-3, a trust root, and the bundle-tier engines T-0045-6, delegated

text.tspan: The diagram's reading of §6, Findings 1 and the Open obligations, with the module headers; not ADR-0068's column

svg.text: Models stay out of the trusted base. The base still grows, on every vehicle (§2). Grouping is the diagram's; the record lists the rows T-0068-1 to 12 in order.

text.tspan: ADR-0045 §2: a component is a row only if its failure can only subtract, or its identity is issued

svg.text: Delegated: its failure can produce only subtractions. No proof, no key, no quorum; declared per deployment.
Trust root: its failure can add, and it is admissible only if both hold: its identity is fixed by an anchor issuance or a promotion, and it entered by a record of its own.
Refused: a component whose failure can add and whose identity neither issuance nor promotion fixes is not a row. It moves inside the verified object, or the design
changes until its failure only subtracts.

text.tspan: Findings 1: four rows meet neither half

svg.text: T-0068-4 a vehicle's measure of an extent, T-0068-7 its position source, T-0068-8 its interlock, T-0068-9 its recovery function.
Their failure can add (an entry past what was voted, an envelope elsewhere, an irreversible effect without a person, expiry with no safe state), and nothing issues
their identity: they are trusted for what their builder says of them (Consequences).
Either an attested identity for each is declared per vehicle class, as ADR-0034 does for a guest, or they are assumptions of use with an owner. The record
lists them as rows and says so.

text.tspan: Finding 2, and where the rows would go (§5)

svg.text: ADR-0045 §4: a deployment "instantiates rows and adds none that is not a degeneracy". An overlay that adds twelve is outside that sentence, one more reason
this is reported upstream and not declared as a rung.
If the archetype takes ADR-0059 to ADR-0067, ADR-0045 owes these rows in its table and a declaration of them in every deployment that seats a governor.
Not an annex to ADR-0045 while this is an overlay ⟨Q11⟩: ADR-0045 is accepted, and an annex would amend it (Options).

A deployment that does not meet one does not inherit what the modules of ADR-0059 to ADR-0066 would prove (§3). The sentence was written before the modules; they now exist, and the cross-reference below says where a module carries an assumption as its premise.

text.tspan: Where a module takes it as a premise

svg.text: The governor is separate from the stack and is the only path to the actuators and the radio
The stack is Mediated, and every property here is void. This is A1 for a vehicle
Federation (Verifiers are honest) and Outstanding (two governors, honest) say so in their headers
Captured and slow replicas together are fewer than a certificate, and each sound clock's margin covers its drift
NoGrantPastExpiry is void. EffectsAfterRevocationBounded is not

The first half is PlaneClock's ClockPremise. The second is folded into a clock's class there ("margins are folded into a clock's class"); the module says nothing of a real clock's drift. Outstanding has no clock
Effect classes are declared as what they are
An irreversible effect is reachable by an agent, or by a governor alone
Each vehicle class has a declared safe state, and its recovery function reaches it in bounded time
The terminal behaviour is a stall, which for a body in motion is not safe
A trained, authorized person is at each release seat and can see what the act requires
HITL is a key and not a judgment
No more replicas of an exposed plane are captured than its current membership tolerates, at every step of its schedule
That plane is captured. It is bounded by its charter or intent, and by each honest governor's account against K_up
Membership's CapturedWithinFloor, with StepAtFloor keeping the tolerance at or above it, at five replicas
What a vehicle does to the world other than through its entries is declared as outside the alphabet
Effect exclusivity is claimed for a body, and is false
Every entry's extent is declared as what it is
A count bounds how many acts and not what they do
PlaneClock models an extent as a number of ticks only
Envelopes, counts and budgets are voted against what every stack could do together
The joint effect of permitted acts is one no tally weighed
T_tick is long against a round of the plane over its radios
Ticks fall behind and leases end, with no adversary present

text.tspan: The diagram's cross-reference to the module headers, not ADR-0068's
ToO rev 15 §13, as ADR-0068 cites it

svg.text: A1: effect exclusivity is enforced by a declared, attested confinement profile. A-0068-1 is "A1 for a vehicle".

A9: the mechanism's replicas are not compromised, crash-recovery. TM4: under crash-recovery consensus one such replica can propose an admit no floor evaluated, which is why ADR-0059 §5 asks for Byzantine agreement.
A13: the cell Observer is not colluding with its Thinker. TM11: coupling cannot see collusion.

If the archetype takes ADR-0059 to ADR-0067, its records owe: ADR-0045, these rows in its table and a declaration of them in every deployment that seats a governor; ToO §13, these assumptions beside A1 to A18.
Until then the overlay declares them here, as ADR-0045's Annex B is the reference's declaration. Carries a debt against: nothing while this is an overlay.

text.tspan: §4 · What is given up, in one place: each record names its own costs, and together

svg.text: No delegation. Planes grant below themselves
A bound in seconds as a theorem. Revocation is bounded in effects, and the bound in duration is declared
An ordered admit before every effect, for every pre-authorized entry and every report to a peer
A person in reach, for a plane that is cut off

text.tspan: Any act by a vehicle that is alone

svg.text: "Not autonomous." No principal seats, delegates to or addresses another, and that stays true. It is no longer true that a person is always on the plane that orders an effect

text.tspan: §6 · Ratification condition, item by item, with the diagram's note on each
ADR-0059 to ADR-0067 are ratified first, or with this record

svg.text: A row for a record that is not ratified is withdrawn with it
None is ratified. All nine are Proposed; ADR-0059 to ADR-0067 were each revised R1 on 2026.11.10

text.tspan: Each row is read against ADR-0045's test: its failure can only subtract, or its identity is

svg.text: Not met. Four rows here are trust roots whose identity nothing issues: a vehicle's measure of an extent, its position source, its interlock and its recovery function. That is a finding
(Findings, 1)
Unchanged by the modules. None models these four: PlaneClock counts an extent in ticks, no module has a position, Release relies on the interlock's checks, and Alone leaves the safe state to physics

text.tspan: Each bound in §1 names a property of a module that exists
Not met: no module is written.

svg.text: Out of date, and not revised. The modules of ADR-0059 to ADR-0066 were written, checked and proved on 2026.11.10 (the modules table at the top). The cross-reference column of §1's table finds a property in a module header for
TM1–TM3, TM5, TM6 and TM12–TM14, several under a premise, and none for TM4 and TM7–TM11. ADR-0068 names none of them, so as written the condition is still not met

text.tspan: A reader who is not the drafter (ADR-0029 A2)

svg.text: And for this record, one who knows vehicles
No reading is recorded: the History has one row, the initial draft

text.tspan: The diagram's note, not ADR-0068's text

svg.text: Not taken while this is an overlay ⟨Q11⟩. ADR-0045 is accepted, and an annex would amend it

text.tspan: The rows spread over the records they belong to

svg.text: Not taken. ADR-0045's rule is one table, so that an undeclared row can be seen to be missing

text.tspan: The corpus's adversary alone, the agent

svg.text: Rejected ⟨3⟩. A link adversary and a captured vehicle are the ordinary case for this deployment

text.tspan: Physical destruction out of scope, as the proposal's first revision had it

svg.text: Not taken. Its effect on a quorum is TM12
One table of what the overlay trusts, and one of what it assumes.
Each adversary has a stated residual, and three of them have "nothing" in the bounding column where that is the truth.
Trust roots nothing issues. A vehicle's position source, its measure of an extent, its interlock and its recovery function are trusted for what their builder says of
them.
Navigation deception is bounded by nothing here (TM8).
Collusion is unseen, as the corpus states it today (TM11).

text.tspan: One author, one day, and no vehicle.

svg.text: 1. ADR-0045 admits a component only if its failure can only subtract, or its identity is issued. Four rows here meet neither as they stand: T-0068-4, T-0068-7,
T-0068-8 and T-0068-9, a vehicle's measure of an extent, its position source, its interlock and its recovery function. Either an attested identity for each is declared per
vehicle class, as ADR-0034 does for a guest, or they are assumptions of use with an owner. The record lists them as rows and says so.
2. A deployment "instantiates rows and adds none that is not a degeneracy" (ADR-0045 §4, in the words of ADR-0058's header). An overlay that adds twelve is
outside that sentence, which is one more reason this is reported upstream and not declared as a rung.
3. Two readings found gaps this record leaves open: a captured vehicle discloses the rules it carries (the NATO reading, F3), and TM3's "once its plane knows"
names no way of knowing (the swarm reading, Z2).
The reading of each row against ADR-0045 (§6), and the disposition of finding 1.
What attests a governor at seating, as ADR-0034 attests a guest. T-0068-1 and T-0068-6 rest on it, and no record of this set says.
A false-finding rate for a plane with nobody in reach, as an availability parameter (the swarm reading, Z3).
An Observer that accuses or vanishes, beside TM11's silent one (the swarm reading, Z4).
A second anchor, for a coalition, which is out of this design (the NATO reading, N2).
Disclosure on capture, as a row or as an adversary's capability in TM3 (the NATO reading, F3).

text.tspan: The diagram's note: what would meet §6's third condition

svg.text: Not listed by the record. An R1 revision of ADR-0068 naming, for each bound in §1, the module property that states it, as the R1 rows of ADR-0059 to ADR-0066
cite their modules, with its Status note brought up to date. Until then the condition reads "not met".
